analysis:
The supplied units are docs and a changelog only. The only security-relevant content is what the text says about an unregistered, opt-in Nemotron Super path; no implementation was supplied. Changelog claims:
- An opt-in image HTTP hook, disabled by default, reuses existing auth, JSON/SSE framing and cancellation.
- The provider decodes consumer-supplied PNG/JPEG in-process via ImageIO and a CPU decoder, with EXIF/XMP orientation and declared-geometry bounds. This is untrusted-input parsing surface (TB-007, A-001).
- Env opt-ins: MTP speculation, MAX_CONCURRENT up to 8, prefill chunk size, and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY (the finding; contradicts the T-041 'no RAM tier' claim, changelog line 57).
- Image requests refuse tools and structured output. A busy owner returns 429.
hardware-support.md (head lines 13-18) adds a statement that the Super builder requires a live pending LOAD lease and preserves the fixed-workspace concurrency floor. That is consistent with the existing memory-admission invariants. The inference.md patch was only partially visible (metadata and an excerpt). Its text mentions the owner draining local text and image bindings in `closeAfterDrain`, request-retirement ownership, and a mismatch-free LOAD recheck. Next pass should check: (1) the HTTP hook auth path and whether any new route is reachable without the coordinator's E2E encryption path (T-008, TB-002); (2) the cacheSalt and scope handling for the checkpoint bank (T-041); (3) the image decoder resource bounds (T-010 DoS); (4) retirement and zeroization of residual GPU state (T-028).

findings.detail: The changelog adds `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, which opts the plain Nemotron Super owner into a resident recurrent checkpoint bank. Its budget is reserved from load until retirement, and a restored request continues from checkpoints at prefill-chunk multiples. T-041 and hardware-support.md state that production never constructs a resident-RAM prefix cache and that encrypted SSD is the sole tier. The visible text does not say how the bank is scoped by the coordinator-authored cacheSalt (account, model build, prompt contract), whether checkpoint contents are encrypted, or how they are wiped at retirement. The bank also adds a cross-request TTFT hit/miss oracle with no TTL. Only the changelog and docs were supplied, so the code is unreviewed. If the bank is ever served beyond a single trusted tenant, hits could cross account scopes. Fix: before enabling, update T-041 and TB-007 to cover this tier (scope key, lifetime, zeroization, same-account-only reuse). Require cacheSalt in the checkpoint key and keep the flag out of any registered or production path.
findings.title: Opt-in resident RAM prefix reuse for Super contradicts the T-041 'no production RAM tier' posture
